faqs.q: What are the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive used for?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive are hexagon sockets that fit a 3/4" square drive, listed in 22 sizes from 3/4" (19mm) to 2" across flats. Match the socket to the hexagon size of the nut or bolt head and to the 3/4" square drive of the wrench.

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive, such as BSH75088?
faqs.a: The part numbers start BSH, then a drive code (75 on the 3/4" drive), then a three-digit hexagon size. That size is in millimetres on metric sockets and in hundredths of an inch on the smaller imperial ones: BSH7519 is the 3/4" (19mm) socket and BSH75200 the 2" socket.

faqs.q: What hexagon sizes do the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive cover?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive cover 22 hexagon sizes, from 3/4" (19mm) up to 2", in imperial and metric sizes with the millimetre size shown for many of them. For example BSH75144 is the 1-7/16" socket.

faqs.q: Are the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive metric or imperial sizes?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive list both. Imperial sizes such as 3/4" (19mm) sit alongside metric sizes written in millimetres, and several rows give both, for example 1-7/16". Choose the row that matches your bolt or nut across flats.

faqs.q: What torque or pressure rating do the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no torque or pressure rating for the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive. A socket is limited by the wrench it is used with, so check the rated torque of your torque wrench and ask us for Enerpac's rating for the socket if your job runs near the wrench limit.

faqs.q: What are the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive made of?
faqs.a: The listing does not state the material of the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive. Ask us for Enerpac's data if your job needs a specific material or heat-treatment, and see our [hydraulic torque wrench guide](/blog/hydraulic-torque-wrenches-guide) for choosing sockets.

faqs.q: Is there a standard or certificate for the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard and attaches no certificate for the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive. Ask us if your project needs a calibration or material certificate, and we request it from Enerpac with the order.

faqs.q: Which wrench do the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive fit?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive fit a wrench with a 3/4" square drive. The listing sorts the sockets by square drive, so check your wrench's drive size first; the other BSH drives are listed as separate products such as the [Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 1" Square Drive](/p/enerpac-bsh-impact-sockets-for-1-in-square-drive).

faqs.q: How should the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive be used and checked?
faqs.a: Seat the socket fully on the nut or bolt head and on the 3/4" drive before you apply torque, and keep the wrench square to the fastener. Check the socket for cracks or rounded corners before use, and replace a damaged one rather than reuse it.

faqs.q: Which socket size should I order for a 1-7/16" nut?
faqs.a: For a 1-7/16" hexagon on a 3/4" drive the part number in the table is BSH75144. Measure the nut across flats to confirm the size, and quote the part number or the hexagon size and drive.

faqs.q: How does the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive range compare with the Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 1" Square Drive?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 3/4" Square Drive are for a 3/4" drive and cover 3/4" (19mm) to 2" in 22 sizes, while the [Enerpac BSH Impact Sockets for 1" Square Drive](/p/enerpac-bsh-impact-sockets-for-1-in-square-drive) are for a 1" drive and cover 3/4" (19mm) to 100mm in 53 sizes. A larger drive takes bigger fasteners, so pick the drive that matches your wrench.

faqs.q: What are the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners used for?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners are back-up spanners that hold a nut or bolt head while the torque wrench works on the other end. The listing has 12 models, each covering a hexagon size range, from 1-1/16" to 1-1/4" (BUS01) up to 4-1/8" to 4-15/16" (BUS11), plus two metric ranges.

faqs.q: How do I choose between the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners part numbers BUS01 to BUS12?
faqs.a: Each part number covers one hexagon size range: BUS01 is 1-1/16" to 1-1/4", BUS02 is 1-7/16" to 1-5/8" and BUS03 is 1-13/16" to 2", and so on up to BUS08 (4-1/4" to 4-5/8"). BUS09 (85 to 90mm) and BUS12 (115 to 120mm) are metric, and BUS10 and BUS11 fill the 3-3/4" to 4-15/16" gap. The numbers are not in size order, so use the range.

faqs.q: What hexagon size ranges do the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners cover?
faqs.a: The twelve ranges run from 1-1/16" to 4-15/16" in imperial sizes and 85 to 120mm in metric sizes. Each spanner covers a band of two or three hexagon sizes, for example 2-3/16" to 2-3/8" on BUS04, so match the band to your nut across flats.

faqs.q: Which metric back-up spanners are in the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners range?
faqs.a: The metric ones are BUS09, which covers 85 to 90mm, and BUS12, which covers 115 to 120mm. The other ten cover imperial hexagon sizes, so for a metric nut outside those bands ask us which spanner fits.

faqs.q: What torque rating do the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners have?
faqs.a: The listing gives no torque rating for the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners. A back-up spanner takes the reaction while the wrench tightens, so ask us for Enerpac's rating for your part number if you are working near the rated torque of your wrench.

faqs.q: What are the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners made of?
faqs.a: The listing does not state the material of the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners. Ask us for Enerpac's data if your job needs a specific material, and see our [hydraulic torque wrench guide](/blog/hydraulic-torque-wrenches-guide) for how back-up spanners are used.

faqs.q: Which wrenches do the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners work with?
faqs.a: The Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners are listed by hexagon size range, not by wrench model, so they work alongside any torque wrench that is tightening a nut or bolt of that size. For the wrench-side reaction parts see the [reaction arms for PTW and ETW wrenches](/p/enerpac-reaction-arms-and-extended-drives-for-ptw-and-etw-torque-wrenches).

faqs.q: How should the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners be used and checked?
faqs.a: Fit the spanner on the fixed end of the bolt so it holds the nut or head while the wrench tightens the other end, and keep it square to the fastener. Check the jaws for wear or cracks before use, and replace a damaged spanner.

faqs.q: Which back-up spanner should I order for a 2-1/2 in. hexagon nut?
faqs.a: For a 2-9/16" to 2-3/4" hexagon the table lists BUS05, and for 2-3/16" to 2-3/8" it lists BUS04. A 2-1/2" hexagon falls between those bands, so measure across flats and ask us which part number fits.

faqs.q: How do back-up spanners differ from reaction arms?
faqs.a: A back-up spanner such as the Enerpac BUS Back-Up Spanners holds the fastener on the far side of the joint, while a [reaction arm](/p/enerpac-reaction-arms-and-extended-reaction-tubes-for-rsl-torque-wrenches) braces the wrench itself against a neighbouring fixed point. Many bolting jobs use one or the other, and the choice depends on access.

faqs.q: How do I read the part numbers of the Enerpac DDA Allen (Hex) Drives for DSX Torque Wrenches, such as DDA110104 and DDA11046?
